from_quote: or even in our bill of rights
rationale: The speaker reports that Mr. Marshall "conceived the trial by jury better secured under the plan on the table than in the British government, or even in our bill of rights".

from_quote: the appellate jurisdiction of the judicial power, both as to law and fact, with such exceptions and under such regulations as Congress shall make
rationale: The paragraph says the speaker "proceeded to state the appellate jurisdiction of the judicial power, both as to law and fact, with such exceptions and under such regulations as Congress shall make".
to_quote: appellate Jurisdiction, both as to Law and Fact, with such Exceptions, and under such Regulations as the Congress shall make

from_quote: as in our bill of rights
rationale: The speaker says he conceived trial by jury "was as well secured, and not better secured, in the proposed new Constitution as in our bill of rights".

from_quote: the ancient trial by jury preserved in the Virginia bill of rights
rationale: The speaker asks "Is not the ancient trial by jury preserved in the Virginia bill of rights?"

from_quote: the difference between the new plan and our bill of rights
rationale: The paragraph says Mr. Henry explained "the difference between the new plan and our bill of rights" and that the latter "had been violated by several acts of Assembly".

from_quote: Full faith and credit shall be given to all acts
rationale: Mr. Mason speaks of "the latter part of this clause" and says "Full faith and credit shall be given to all acts"; the preceding record says the first section of the fourth article was read.
to_quote: Full Faith and Credit shall be given in each State to the public Acts
